title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 118 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 584–587 (Night 118, continuing directly from nights-117), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 118 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. ʿAzīz goes on with his tale to Tāj al-Mulūk. Holding his eyes open in the garden, he grows hungry, eats, drinks ten cups of wine and falls senseless; he wakes outside the garden with a knife and an iron dirham on his belly. His cousin ʿAzīza reads the signs: the lady swears by her right eye that if he comes back and sleeps again she will cut his throat. She feeds him, lets him sleep through the day while she fans him in tears, and sends him back with one charge: to recite to the lady, as he leaves her, the line of verse she gave him. This time he stays awake; the lady comes at the end of the night with ten slave-girls, finds him watching, and the two spend the night together, a scene the text tells frankly and this translation renders in full. In the morning, as he turns to go, she holds him back to tell him something. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the eighteenth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and eighteenth night,
sentences.n: al-thāminata ʿashara, “eighteenth”: as in the nights before, the print has the masculine عشر beside the feminine night, and it is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ قَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَدَخَلْتُ الْبُسْتَانَ وَطَلَعْتُ ذَلِكَ الْمَقْعَدَ وَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَجَعَلْتُ أَفْتَحُ عَيْنِي بِأَصَابِعِي وَأَهُزُّ رَأْسِي حِينَ جَنَّ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba qāla li-tāji al-mulūki fa-dakhaltu al-bustāna wa-ṭalaʿtu dhālika al-maqʿada wa-naẓartu ilā al-bustāni wa-jaʿaltu aftaḥu ʿaynī bi-aṣābiʿī wa-ahuzzu raʾsī ḥīna janna al-laylu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the youth said to Tāj al-Mulūk: And I entered the garden, and went-up (into) that sitting-place, and looked at the garden; and I began opening my eye with my fingers and shaking my head, when the night grew-dark.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man said to Tāj al-Mulūk: I went into the garden, climbed up into the alcove and looked out over the garden, and as darkness fell I kept holding my eyes open with my fingers and shaking my head.
sentences.n: The night opens by going back over the last lines of the night before. bi-aṣābiʿī, “with my fingers”: bi- of the instrument.

sentences.t: فَجُعْتُ مِنَ السَّهَرِ وَهَبَّتْ عَلَيَّ رَوَائِحُ الطَّعَامِ فَازْدَادَ جُوعِي وَتَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَى السُّفْرَةِ وَكَشَفْتُ غِطَاوَهَا وَأَكَلْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ لَوْنٍ لُقْمَةً وَأَكَلْتُ قِطْعَةَ لَحْمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-juʿtu mina al-sahari wa-habbat ʿalayya rawāʾiḥu al-ṭaʿāmi fa-izdāda jūʿī wa-tawajjahtu ilā al-sufrati wa-kashaftu ghiṭāwahā wa-akaltu min kulli lawnin luqmatan wa-akaltu qiṭʿata laḥmin
sentences.l: And I hungered from the wakefulness, and the smells of the food blew upon me, and my hunger increased; and I turned-towards the food-cloth, and uncovered its cover, and ate from every kind a mouthful, and ate a piece of meat.
sentences.i: The long watch made me hungry, and the smell of the food drifted over to me, and my hunger grew; so I went to the spread, lifted its cover, ate a mouthful of every dish, and ate a piece of meat.
sentences.n: ghiṭāwahā, “its cover”: the print spells غطاوها, with a wāw for the hamza of ghiṭāʾ, a spoken form; Classical writes غطاءها. sufra: the cloth or tray on which a meal is laid out. lawn, “colour”, is here “kind, dish”.

sentences.t: وَأَتَيْتُ إِلَى بَاطِيَةِ الْخَمْرِ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي أَشْرَبُ قَدَحًا فَشَرِبْتُهُ ثُمَّ شَرِبْتُ الثَّانِيَ وَالثَّالِثَ إِلَى غَايَةِ عَشَرَةٍ وَقَدْ ضَرَبَنِي الْهَوَاءُ فَوَقَعْتُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ كَالْقَتِيلِ
sentences.tr: wa-ataytu ilā bāṭiyati al-khamri wa-qultu fī nafsī ashrabu qadaḥan fa-sharibtuhu thumma sharibtu al-thāniya wa-al-thālitha ilā ghāyati ʿasharatin wa-qad ḍarabanī al-hawāʾu fa-waqaʿtu ʿalā al-arḍi ka-al-qatīli
sentences.l: And I came to the flagon of the wine, and said in myself: I-will-drink a cup; and I drank it, then I drank the second and the third, up to the limit of ten; and the air had struck me, and I fell on the ground like the slain.
sentences.i: Then I went to the flagon of wine and said to myself, “I will drink one cup.” I drank it, and then a second and a third, until I had drunk ten; by then the air had gone to my head, and I dropped to the ground like a dead man.
sentences.n: ḍarabanī al-hawāʾu, “the air struck me”: the night air on top of the wine, which sets a drinker reeling; a common way of saying the wine went to his head. ilā ghāyati ʿasharatin, “up to the limit of ten”: as many as ten cups. ka-al-qatīli, “like the slain”: ka- of likeness.

sentences.t: وَمَازِلْتُ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى طَلَعَ النَّهَارُ فَانْتَبَهْتُ فَرَأَيْتُ نَفْسِي خَارِجَ الْبُسْتَانِ وَعَلَى بَطْنِي شَفْرَةٌ مَاضِيَةٌ وَدِرْهَمُ حَدِيدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-mā ziltu ka-dhālika ḥattā ṭalaʿa al-nahāru fa-intabahtu fa-raʾaytu nafsī khārija al-bustāni wa-ʿalā baṭnī shafratun māḍiyatun wa-dirhamu ḥadīdin
sentences.l: And I ceased not thus until the day rose; and I woke, and saw myself outside the garden, and on my belly a blade sharp and a dirham of iron.
sentences.i: There I lay until daylight; and when I woke I found myself outside the garden, with a keen blade and an iron dirham lying on my belly.
sentences.n: wa-mā ziltu, “and I did not cease”, is printed as one word. shafra: a broad blade, a knife; the print points the first two letters. A dirham is a silver coin; this one is of iron, so it is a sign, not money.

sentences.t: فَارْتَجَفْتُ وَأَخَذْتُهُمَا وَأَتَيْتُ بِهِمَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فَوَجَدْتُ ابْنَةَ عَمِّي تَقُولُ إِنِّي فِي هَذَا الْبَيْتِ مِسْكِينَةٌ حَزِينَةٌ لَيْسَ لِي مُعِينٌ إِلَّا الْبُكَاءُ
sentences.tr: fa-irtajaftu wa-akhadhtuhumā wa-ataytu bihimā ilā al-bayti fa-wajadtu ibnata ʿammī taqūlu innī fī hādhā al-bayti miskīnatun ḥazīnatun laysa lī muʿīnun illā al-bukāʾu
sentences.l: And I trembled, and took the two, and came with them to the house, and found the daughter of my uncle saying: I in this house am wretched, sorrowful; there is not for me a helper except the weeping.
sentences.i: I shuddered, picked them both up and brought them home, and found my cousin saying, “In this house I am wretched and sorrowful, and I have no help but weeping.”
sentences.n: atā bi-, “come with”, is “bring”: ataytu bihimā, “I brought the two of them”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ وَقَعْتُ مِنْ طُولِى وَرَمَيْتُ السِّكِّينَ وَالدِّرْهَمَ مِنْ يَدِي وَغُشِيَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu waqaʿtu min ṭūlī wa-ramaytu al-sikkīna wa-al-dirhama min yadī wa-ghushiya ʿalayya
sentences.l: And when I entered, I fell from my length, and threw the knife and the dirham from my hand, and it was fainted upon me.
sentences.i: As I came in I fell full length, flinging the knife and the dirham from my hand, and I fainted.
sentences.n: waqaʿtu min ṭūlī, “I fell from my length”: fell headlong, full length; طولى is printed with ى for final ي. ghushiya ʿalayya, “it was covered over me”: the usual impersonal passive for fainting. The blade (shafra) is now called sikkīn, “knife”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَقْتُ مِنْ غَشْيَتِي عَرَّفْتُهَا بِمَا حَصَلَ لِي وَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّنِي لَمْ أَنَلْ أَرَبِي فَاشْتَدَّ حُزْنُهَا عَلَيَّ لَمَّارَأَتْ بُكَائِي وَوَجْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afaqtu min ghashyatī ʿarraftuhā bi-mā ḥaṣala lī wa-qultu lahā innanī lam anal arabī fa-ishtadda ḥuznuhā ʿalayya lammā raʾat bukāʾī wa-wajdī
sentences.l: And when I recovered from my faint, I made-her-know of what had befallen me, and said to her: I have not attained my aim. And her grief over me grew-severe when she saw my weeping and my passion.
sentences.i: When I came round from my faint I told her all that had happened to me and said, “I have not got what I wanted.” Her grief for me grew sharper when she saw me weeping and so full of longing.
sentences.n: ʿarrafa bi-, “make known”: the bi- marks the thing told (bi-mā, “of what”). arab: need, aim, desire. lammā raʾat, “when she saw”, is printed as one word, لمارات. wajd: the passion of love, ardent longing.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِي إِنِّي عَجَزْتُ وَأَنَا أَنْصَحُكَ عَنِ النَّوْمِ فَلَمْ تَسْمَعْ نُصْحِي فَكَلَامِي لَا يُفِيدُكَ شَيْاً
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lī innī ʿajaztu wa-anā anṣaḥuka ʿani al-nawmi fa-lam tasmaʿ nuṣḥī fa-kalāmī lā yufīduka shayʾan
sentences.l: And she said to me: I have become-powerless while I counsel you against the sleep, and you did not hear my counsel; so my speech does not profit you a thing.
sentences.i: And she said to me, “I have worn myself out warning you against sleep, and you would not listen to my advice; nothing I say does you any good.”
sentences.n: ʿajaztu wa-anā anṣaḥuka, “I have grown helpless while I counsel you”: I am worn out with counselling you. شياً is the edition’s spelling of shayʾan, “a thing”, without the hamza.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَسْأَلُكِ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ تُفَسِّرِي لِي إِشَارَةَ السِّكِّينِ وَالدِّرْهَمِ الْحَدِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā asʾaluki bi-allāhi an tufassirī lī ishārata al-sikkīni wa-al-dirhami al-ḥadīdi
sentences.l: And I said to her: I ask you by God that you interpret for me the sign of the knife and the dirham the iron.
sentences.i: I said to her, “I beg you, by God, explain to me what the knife and the iron dirham mean.”
sentences.n: bi-allāhi, “by God”: bi- of the oath. al-dirham al-ḥadīd, “the iron dirham”: the noun ḥadīd, “iron”, stands as an adjective after the noun, a loose spoken construction.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَمَّا الدِّرْهَمُ الْحَدِيدُ فَإِنَّهَا تُشِيرُ بِهِ إِلَى عَيْنِهَا الْيَمِينِ وَإِنَّهَا تُقْسِمُ بِهَا وَتَقُولُ وَحَقِّ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَعَيْنِي الْيَمِينِ إِنْ رَجَعْتَ ثَانِيَ مَرَّةٍ وَنِمْتَ لَأَذْبَحَنَّكَ بِهَذِهِ السِّكِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ammā al-dirhamu al-ḥadīdu fa-innahā tushīru bihi ilā ʿaynihā al-yamīni wa-innahā tuqsimu bihā wa-taqūlu wa-ḥaqqi rabbi al-ʿālamīna wa-ʿaynī al-yamīni in rajaʿta thāniya marratin wa-nimta la-adhbaḥannaka bi-hādhihi al-sikkīni
sentences.l: And she said: As for the dirham the iron, she points with it to her eye the right, and she swears by it and says: By the right of the Lord of the worlds and my eye the right, if you return a second time and sleep, I will surely slaughter you with this knife.
sentences.i: She said, “The iron dirham: with it she points to her right eye, and she swears by that eye, saying, ‘By the Lord of the worlds and by my right eye, if you come back a second time and fall asleep, I will cut your throat with this knife.’
sentences.n: The coin stands for her eye; perhaps there is also a play on ʿayn, which means both “eye” and “coin, ready money”. tushīru bihi, “she points with it”: bi- of the instrument; tuqsimu bihā, “she swears by it”: bi- of the oath. wa-ḥaqqi, “by the right of”: wa- of the oath. al-yamīn, “the right”, stands as an adjective beside the feminine ʿayn, where Classical says al-yumnā. la-adhbaḥannaka: la- of the oath with the energetic ending, “I will surely slaughter you”; the print points the shadda. The knife is feminine here (hādhihi al-sikkīn), as it often is.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا خَائِفَةٌ عَلَيْكَ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي مِنْ مَكْرِهَا وَقَلْبِي مَلْآنُ بِالْحُزْنِ عَلَيْكَ فَمَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā khāʾifatun ʿalayka yā bna ʿammī min makrihā wa-qalbī malʾānu bi-al-ḥuzni ʿalayka fa-mā aqdiru an atakallama
sentences.l: And I am fearful for you, O son of my uncle, from her cunning, and my heart is full with the grief over you, so I am not able that I speak.
sentences.i: I fear her cunning for you, cousin, and my heart is so full of grief for you that I cannot speak.
sentences.n: khāʾifa ʿalā … min, “afraid for (someone) of (something)”. bi-al-ḥuzni, “with grief”: the bi- says what the heart is full of. malʾān, “full”, is a diptote and takes no tanwīn. يا بن is written without the alif of ibn, as usual after yā.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْرِفُ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ أَنَّكَ إِنْ رَجَعْتَ إِلَيْهَا لَا تَنَامُ فَارْجِعْ إِلَيْهَا وَاحْذَرِ النَّوْمَ فَإِنَّكَ تَفُوزُ بِحَاجَتِكَ وَإِنْ عَرَفْتَ أَنَّكَ إِنْ رَجَعْتَ إِلَيْهَا تَنَامُ عَلَى عَادَتِكَ ثُمَّ رَجَعْتَ إِلَيْهَا وَنِمْتَ ذَبَحَتْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in kunta taʿrifu min nafsika annaka in rajaʿta ilayhā lā tanāmu fa-irjiʿ ilayhā wa-iḥdhari al-nawma fa-innaka tafūzu bi-ḥājatika wa-in ʿarafta annaka in rajaʿta ilayhā tanāmu ʿalā ʿādatika thumma rajaʿta ilayhā wa-nimta dhabaḥatka
sentences.l: So if you know of yourself that you, if you return to her, will not sleep, then return to her and beware the sleep, for you will win your need; but if you know that you, if you return to her, will sleep according to your habit, and then you return to her and sleep, she will slaughter you.
sentences.i: If you know yourself well enough to be sure that you will not fall asleep when you go back to her, then go back, and beware of sleep, and you will have what you want. But if you know that you will fall asleep as you always do, and you go back to her and sleep, she will kill you.”
sentences.n: The print has ذبحنك, a misprint for ذبحتك, dhabaḥatka, “she will slaughter you”, corrected here. fāza bi-, “win, attain”: the bi- marks the thing won. Perfect verbs after in, “if”, carry a future sense.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَكَيْفَ يَكُونُ الْعَمَلُ يَا بِنْتَ عَمِّي أَسْأَلُكِ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ تُسَاعِدِينِي فِي هَذِهِ الْبَلِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā wa-kayfa yakūnu al-ʿamalu yā binta ʿammī asʾaluki bi-allāhi an tusāʿidīnī fī hādhihi al-baliyyati
sentences.l: And I said to her: And how is the doing, O daughter of my uncle? I ask you by God that you help me in this affliction.
sentences.i: I said to her, “Then what am I to do, cousin? I beg you, by God, help me in this trouble.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عَلَى عَيْنِي وَرَأْسِي وَلَكِنْ إِنْ سَمِعْتَ كَلَامِي وَأَطَعْتَ أَمْرِي قَضَيْتَ حَاجَتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿalā ʿaynī wa-raʾsī wa-lākin in samiʿta kalāmī wa-aṭaʿta amrī qaḍayta ḥājataka
sentences.l: And she said: On my eye and my head! But if you hear my speech and obey my command, you will accomplish your need.
sentences.i: She said, “With all my heart. But if you listen to what I say and do as I tell you, you will have what you want.”
sentences.n: ʿalā ʿaynī wa-raʾsī, “on my eye and my head”: gladly, at your service.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنِّي أَسْمَعُ كَلَامَكِ وَأُطِيعُ أَمْرَكِ فَقَالَتْ إِذَا كَانَ وَقْتُ الرَّوَاحِ أَقُولُ لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā innī asmaʿu kalāmaki wa-uṭīʿu amraki fa-qālat idhā kāna waqtu al-rawāḥi aqūlu laka
sentences.l: And I said to her: I hear your speech and obey your command. And she said: When it is the time of the going, I will tell you.
sentences.i: I said to her, “I will listen to you and do as you say.” She said, “When it is time for you to go, I will tell you.”
sentences.n: rawāḥ: going out in the evening.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ضَمَّتْنِي إِلَى حِضْنِهَا وَوَضَعَتْنِي عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ وَلَا زَالَتْ تَكْبِسُنِي حَتَّى غَلَبَنِي النُّعَاسُ وَاسْتَغْرَقْتُ فِى النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḍammatnī ilā ḥiḍnihā wa-waḍaʿatnī ʿalā al-firāshi wa-lā zālat takbisunī ḥattā ghalabanī al-nuʿāsu wa-istaghraqtu fī al-nawmi
sentences.l: Then she pressed me to her bosom and laid me on the bed, and did not cease pressing-me until the drowsiness overcame me and I was drowned in the sleep.
sentences.i: Then she held me to her breast and laid me on the bed, and kept rubbing my limbs until drowsiness overcame me and I sank deep in sleep.
sentences.n: kabasa: to press, to knead the limbs, to massage. lā zālat with an imperfect: “she kept on …”. فى is printed with ى for final ي.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ مِرْوَحَةً وَجَلَسَتْ عِنْدَ رَأْسِي تُرَوِّحُ عَلَى وَجْهِي إِلَى آخِرِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat mirwaḥatan wa-jalasat ʿinda raʾsī turawwiḥu ʿalā wajhī ilā ākhiri al-nahāri
sentences.l: And she took a fan, and sat at my head, fanning upon my face until the end of the day.
sentences.i: She took a fan and sat by my head, fanning my face until the end of the day.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَبَّهَتْنِي فَلَمَّا انْتَبَهْتُ وَجَدتُّهَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي وَفِي يَدِهَا الْمِرْوَحَةُ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي وَدُمُوعُهَا قَدْ بَلَّتْ ثِيَابَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma nabbahatnī fa-lammā intabahtu wajattuhā ʿinda raʾsī wa-fī yadihā al-mirwaḥatu wa-hiya tabkī wa-dumūʿuhā qad ballat thiyābahā
sentences.l: Then she woke me; and when I woke I found her at my head, and in her hand the fan, and she weeping, and her tears had wetted her clothes.
sentences.i: Then she woke me, and when I woke I found her sitting by my head with the fan in her hand, weeping, her clothes wet with her tears.
sentences.n: وجدتّها: the print sets a shadda on the tāʾ, showing the dāl of wajadtu run into it as it is spoken: wajattuhā, “I found her”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي اسْتَيْقَظْتُ مَسَحَتْ دُمُوعَهَا وَجَاءَتْ بِشَئٍ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ فَامْتَنَعْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī istayqaẓtu masaḥat dumūʿahā wa-jāʾat bi-shayʾin mina al-akli fa-imtanaʿtu minhu
sentences.l: And when she saw me (that) I had woken, she wiped her tears and came with something of the food, and I refused it.
sentences.i: When she saw that I was awake she wiped away her tears and brought me something to eat, but I would not touch it.
sentences.n: raʾatnī istayqaẓtu, “she saw me — I had woken”: the second verb follows with no joining word, a loose spoken construction. jāʾat bi-, “came with”, is “brought”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي أَمَا قُلْتُ لَكَ اسْمَعْ مِنِّى وَكُلْ فَأَكَلْتُ وَلَمْ أُخَالِفْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī a-mā qultu laka ismaʿ minnī wa-kul fa-akaltu wa-lam ukhālifhā
sentences.l: And she said to me: Did I not say to you: Hear from me? And eat! And I ate, and did not oppose her.
sentences.i: She said to me, “Did I not tell you to listen to me? Now eat.” So I ate, and did not cross her.
sentences.n: a-mā, “did … not?”: the question particle a- with the negative mā. The print points the ḍamma of kul, “eat!”. منى is printed with ى for final ي.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتْ تَضَعُ الْأَكْلَ فِي فَمِي وَأَنَا أَمْضَغُ حَتَّى امْتَلَأْتُ ثُمَّ أَسْقَتْنِي نَقِيعَ عُنَّابٍ بِالسُّكَّرِ ثُمَّ غَسَلَتْ يَدِى وَنَشَّفَتْهَا بِمَحْرَمَةٍ وَرَشَّتْ عَلَيَّ مَاءَ الْوَرْدِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat taḍaʿu al-akla fī famī wa-anā amḍaghu ḥattā imtalaʾtu thumma asqatnī naqīʿa ʿunnābin bi-al-sukkari thumma ghasalat yadī wa-nashshafathā bi-maḥramatin wa-rashshat ʿalayya māʾa al-wardi
sentences.l: And she took-to putting the food in my mouth while I chewed, until I was filled; then she gave-me-to-drink an infusion of jujube with the sugar; then she washed my hand and dried it with a napkin, and sprinkled on me the water of the rose.
sentences.i: She set about putting the food into my mouth while I chewed, until I was full; then she gave me jujubes steeped in water and sweetened with sugar to drink, washed my hand and dried it with a napkin, and sprinkled me with rosewater.
sentences.n: ṣārat with an imperfect: “she began to …”. naqīʿ: fruit steeped in water, a sherbet; ʿunnāb, the jujube. bi-al-sukkari, “with sugar”: bi- of what goes with it; the print points the shadda and the final kasra. maḥrama: a napkin or handkerchief. يدى is printed with ى; it is read yadī, “my hand”, since the next verb (nashshafathā, “she dried it”) has a singular object.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْتُ مَعَهَا وَأَنَا فِي عَافِيَةٍ فَلَمَّا أَظْلَمَ اللَّيْلُ أَلْبَسَتْنِي ثِيَابِي وَقَالَتْ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي اسْهَرْ جَمِيعَ اللَّيْلِ وَلَا تَنَمْ فَإِنَّهَا مَا تَأْتِيكَ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ إِلَّا فِى آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-jalastu maʿahā wa-anā fī ʿāfiyatin fa-lammā aẓlama al-laylu albasatnī thiyābī wa-qālat yā bna ʿammī ismar jamīʿa al-layli wa-lā tanam fa-innahā mā taʾtīka fī hādhihi al-laylati illā fī ākhiri al-layli
sentences.l: And I sat with her, and I in good-health; and when the night grew-dark, she clothed me in my clothes and said: O son of my uncle, stay-awake all the night and do not sleep, for she will not come to you in this night except at the end of the night.
sentences.i: I sat with her, well again; and when night darkened she dressed me in my clothes and said, “Cousin, stay awake the whole night and do not sleep, for tonight she will not come to you until the very end of the night.
sentences.n: lā tanam: lā with the jussive is the prohibition, “do not sleep”. mā taʾtīka, “she will not come to you”: mā negating the imperfect, the spoken way of putting it.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَجْتَمِعُ بِهَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَلَكِنْ لَاتَنْسَ وَصِيَّتِي ثُمَّ بَكَتْ فَأَوْجَعَنِي قَلْبِي عَلَيْهَا مِنْ كَثْرَةِ بُكَائِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-in shāʾa allāhu tajtamiʿu bihā fī hādhihi al-laylati wa-lākin lā tansa waṣiyyatī thumma bakat fa-awjaʿanī qalbī ʿalayhā min kathrati bukāʾihā
sentences.l: And if God wills, you will meet with her in this night; but do not forget my charge. Then she wept, and my heart pained me over her from the abundance of her weeping.
sentences.i: God willing, you will be with her tonight; but do not forget what I told you.” Then she wept, and my heart ached for her, she wept so much.
sentences.n: ijtamaʿa bi-, “meet with, be united with”: the verb takes bi- for the person met. lā tansa, “do not forget”, is printed as one word. waṣiyya: a charge, a parting instruction.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهَا مَا الْوَصِيَّةُ الَّتِي وَعَدْتِنِي بِهَا فَقَالَتْ لِي إِذَا انْصَرَفْتَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا فَأَنْشِدْهَا الْبَيْتَ الْمُتَقَدِّمَ ذِكْرُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahā mā al-waṣiyyatu allatī waʿadtinī bihā fa-qālat lī idhā inṣarafta min ʿindihā fa-anshidhā al-bayta al-mutaqaddima dhikruhu
sentences.l: And I said to her: What is the charge which you promised me? And she said to me: When you depart from her presence, recite-to-her the verse whose mention went-before.
sentences.i: I said to her, “What is this charge you promised me?” She said, “When you are leaving her, recite to her the line of verse I gave you before.”
sentences.n: waʿada bi-, “promise”: the thing promised takes bi-. al-bayt al-mutaqaddim dhikruhu, “the verse whose mention went before”: the line ʿAzīza gave him on an earlier night for the beloved. anshada takes two objects: anshidhā al-bayta, “recite to her the verse”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا وَأَنَا فَرْحَانُ وَمَضَيْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَطَلَعْتُ الْمَقْعَدَ وَأَنَا شَبْعَانُ فَجَلَسْتُ وَسَهِرْتُ إِلَى رُبْعِ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajtu min ʿindihā wa-anā farḥānu wa-maḍaytu ilā al-bustāni wa-ṭalaʿtu al-maqʿada wa-anā shabʿānu fa-jalastu wa-sahirtu ilā rubʿi al-layli
sentences.l: Then I went out from her presence, and I glad, and went-off to the garden, and went-up the sitting-place, and I full-fed; and I sat, and stayed-awake to a quarter of the night.
sentences.i: Then I left her, glad at heart, and went off to the garden and climbed up into the alcove with my stomach full; I sat down and kept awake for a quarter of the night.
sentences.n: farḥān and shabʿān, “glad” and “full”: adjectives of the faʿlān pattern, diptotes, here in a rhyming pair. The print points the ḍamma of kharajtu.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَالَ اللَّيْلُ عَلَيَّ حَتَّى كَأَنَّهُ سَنَةٌ فَمَكَثْتُ سَاهِرًا حَتَّى مَضَي ثَلٰثَةُ أَرْبَاعِ اللَّيْلِ وَصَاحَتِ الدُّيُوكُ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭāla al-laylu ʿalayya ḥattā ka-annahu sanatun fa-makathtu sāhiran ḥattā maḍā thalāthatu arbāʿi al-layli wa-ṣāḥati al-duyūku
sentences.l: Then the night grew-long upon me, until (it was) as though it were a year; and I remained wakeful until three quarters of the night had passed, and the cocks crowed.
sentences.i: Then the night dragged on for me until it seemed a year; and I stayed awake until three quarters of the night were gone and the cocks were crowing.
sentences.n: مضي is printed with a dotted yāʾ for the alif maqṣūra of maḍā, “passed”; ثلثة is the old defective spelling of thalātha, “three”, read with a dagger alif. ka-annahu, “as though it”: ka- of likeness with anna.

sentences.t: فَاشْتَدَّ عِنْدِى الْجُوعُ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ السَّهَرِ فَقُمْتُ إِلَى السُّفْرَةِ وَأَكَلْتُ حَتَّى اكْتَفَيْتُ فَثَقُلَتْ رَأْسِي وَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-ishtadda ʿindī al-jūʿu min kathrati al-sahari fa-qumtu ilā al-sufrati wa-akaltu ḥattā iktafaytu fa-thaqulat raʾsī wa-aradtu an anāma
sentences.l: And the hunger grew-severe with me from the much wakefulness; and I rose to the food-cloth and ate until I had-enough, and my head grew-heavy, and I wanted to sleep.
sentences.i: With all that watching my hunger grew fierce, so I went over to the spread and ate till I was satisfied; my head grew heavy and I longed to sleep.
sentences.n: thaqulat raʾsī, “my head grew heavy”: the verb is feminine, treating raʾs, “head”, as feminine, a spoken usage; Classical makes it masculine. عندى is printed with ى for final ي.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا أَنَا بِنُورٍ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى بُعْدٍ فَنَهَضْتُ وَغَسَلْتُ يَدِي وَفَمِي وَنَبَّهْتُ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-idhā anā bi-nūrin aqbala ʿalā buʿdin fa-nahaḍtu wa-ghasaltu yadī wa-famī wa-nabbahtu nafsī
sentences.l: And behold, I (was) with a light (that) came-forward at a distance; and I rose, and washed my hand and my mouth, and roused myself.
sentences.i: And then, all at once, I saw a light coming towards me from far off; I sprang up, washed my hands and mouth, and shook myself awake.
sentences.n: wa-idhā anā bi-…, “and behold, I (was) with …”: the idhā of surprise; the bi- only marks what suddenly appears. ʿalā buʿdin, “at a distance”.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ وَإِذَا بِهَا أَتَتْ وَمَعَهَا عَشْرُ جَوَارٍ وَهِيَ بَيْنَهُنَّ كَالْبَدْرِ بَيْنَ الْكَوَاكِبِ وَعَلَيْهَا حُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَطْلَسِ الْأَخْضَرِ مُزَرْكَشَةٌ بِالذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ وَهِيَ كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna illā qalīlun wa-idhā bihā atat wa-maʿahā ʿashru jawārin wa-hiya baynahunna ka-al-badri bayna al-kawākibi wa-ʿalayhā ḥullatun mina al-aṭlasi al-akhḍari muzarkashatun bi-al-dhahabi al-aḥmari wa-hiya kamā qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And there was only a little (while), and behold her — she came, and with her ten slave-girls, and she among them like the full-moon among the stars; and on her a robe of the satin the green, embroidered with the gold the red; and she (was) as the poet said:
sentences.i: It was only a little while before there she was, with ten slave-girls about her, and she among them like the full moon among the stars. She wore a robe of green satin embroidered in red gold, and she was as the poet said:
sentences.n: mā kāna illā qalīlun, “there was nothing but a little (while)”: kāna here means “there was”, so qalīl stands in the nominative. wa-idhā bihā, “and behold, she”: the bi- of surprise again. jawārin, “slave-girls”, plural of jāriya. muzarkasha bi-, “embroidered with”: bi- of the material; al-dhahab al-aḥmar, “red gold”, is the usual phrase for pure gold. ka-al-badri, “like the full moon”: ka- of likeness.

sentences.t:
تَتِيهُ عَلَى الْعُشَّاقِ فِي حُلَلٍ خُضْرٍ * مُفَكَّكَةُ الْاَزْرَارِ مَحْلُولَةُ الشَّعْرِ
فَقُلْتُ لَهَا مَا الْاِسْمُ قَالَتْ اَنَا الَّتِي * كَوَيْتُ قُلُوبَ الْعَاشِقِينَ عَلَى الْجَمْرِ
شَكَوْتُ اِلَيْهَا مَا اُقَاسِي مِنَ الْهَوَى * فَقَالَتْ اِلَى صَخْرٍ شَكَوْتَ وَلَمْ تَدْرِ
فَقُلْتُ لَهَا اِنْ كَانَ قَلْبُكَ صَخْرَةً * فَقَدْ اَنْبَعَ اللّٰهُ الزُّلَالَ مِنَ الصَّخْرِ
sentences.tr:
tatīhu ʿalā al-ʿushshāqi fī ḥulalin khuḍrin * mufakkakatu al-azrāri maḥlūlatu al-shaʿri
fa-qultu lahā mā al-ismu qālat anā allatī * kawaytu qulūba al-ʿāshiqīna ʿalā al-jamri
shakawtu ilayhā mā uqāsī mina al-hawā * fa-qālat ilā ṣakhrin shakawta wa-lam tadri
fa-qultu lahā in kāna qalbuka ṣakhratan * fa-qad anbaʿa allāhu al-zulāla mina al-ṣakhri
sentences.l:
She bears-herself-proudly over the lovers in robes green, * unfastened of the buttons, loosened of the hair.
And I said to her: What is the name? She said: I am she who * branded the hearts of the lovers upon the embers.
I complained to her of what I suffer from the passion; * and she said: To a rock you have complained, and you knew not.
And I said to her: If your heart is a rock, * then God has made-gush the sweet-water from the rock.
sentences.i:
She walks in pride among her lovers, robed in green, * her buttons all undone, her hair let loose.
“What is your name?” I asked her. “I am she,” she said, * “who seared the hearts of lovers on the coals.”
I told her all the pain I suffer for her love; * she said, “It is a rock you plead with, and you never knew.”
I said, “And if your heart should be a rock, * yet God made sweet clear water spring from rock.”
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed. tāha ʿalā: to bear oneself proudly towards someone. qalbuka: the print gives the masculine “your”, as Arabic love poetry often speaks of the beloved in the masculine. The last line recalls the rock from which God made water gush for Moses and his people. zulāl: cool, sweet, clear water.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي ضَحِكَتْ وَقَالَتْ كَيْفَ انْتَبَهْتَ وَلَمْ يَغْلِبْ عَلَيْكَ النَّوْمُ وَحَيْثُ سَهِرْتَ اللَّيْلَ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكَ عَاشِقٌ لِأَنَّ مِنْ شِيَمِ الْعُشَّاقِ سَهَرَ اللَّيْلِ فِي مُكَابَدَةِ الْأَشْوَاقِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī ḍaḥikat wa-qālat kayfa intabahta wa-lam yaghlib ʿalayka al-nawmu wa-ḥaythu sahirta al-layla ʿalimtu annaka ʿāshiqun li-anna min shiyami al-ʿushshāqi sahara al-layli fī mukābadati al-ashwāqi
sentences.l: And when she saw me she laughed and said: How (is it) you are awake, and the sleep has not overcome you? And since you have kept-awake the night, I know that you are a lover; because of the natures of the lovers is the waking of the night in the enduring of the longings.
sentences.i: When she saw me she laughed and said, “How is it that you are awake, and sleep has not got the better of you? Since you have watched the night through, I know you are a lover; for it is the way of lovers to lie awake all night, wrestling with their longings.”
sentences.n: ḥaythu, “where”, is used for “since, seeing that”, a common later usage. The print points the ḍamma of ʿalimtu. shiyam: natures, habits. mukābada: enduring, struggling against hardship. ʿushshāq and ashwāq, “lovers” and “longings”, rhyme: a touch of rhymed prose.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَى الْجَوَارِي وَغَمَزَتْهُنَّ فَانْصَرَفْنَ عَنْهَا وَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيَّ وَحَضَنَتْنِي لِصَدْرِهَا وَبَاسَتْنِي وَبُسْتُهَا وَمَصَّتْ شَفَتِي الْفَوْقَانِيَّةَ وَمَصَصْتُ شَفَتَهَا التَّحْتَانِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbalat ʿalā al-jawārī wa-ghamazathunna fa-inṣarafna ʿanhā wa-aqbalat ʿalayya wa-ḥaḍanatnī li-ṣadrihā wa-bāsatnī wa-bustuhā wa-maṣṣat shafatī al-fawqāniyyata wa-maṣaṣtu shafatahā al-taḥtāniyyata
sentences.l: Then she turned to the slave-girls and winked at them, and they went-away from her; and she turned to me, and embraced me to her breast, and kissed me, and I kissed her, and she sucked my lip the upper, and I sucked her lip the lower.
sentences.i: Then she turned to the slave-girls and gave them a wink, and they left her; and she turned to me, clasped me to her breast and kissed me, and I kissed her, and she sucked my upper lip and I sucked her lower lip.
sentences.n: bāsa, “kiss”, is the spoken verb (bustu, “I kissed”), where Classical says qabbala; fawqānī and taḥtānī, “upper” and “lower”, are spoken forms too. li-ṣadrihā, “to her breast”: li- of direction. aqbala ʿalā: to turn towards someone.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَدَدْتُ يَدِي إِلَى خَصْرِهَا وَغَمَزْتُهُ وَمَا نَزَلْنَا فِى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا سَوَاءً وَحَلَّتْ سَرَاوِيلَهَا فَنَزَلَتْ فِي خَلَاخِلِ رِجْلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma madadtu yadī ilā khaṣrihā wa-ghamaztuhu wa-mā nazalnā fī al-arḍi illā sawāʾan wa-ḥallat sarāwīlahā fa-nazalat fī khalākhili rijlayhā
sentences.l: Then I stretched my hand to her waist and pressed it, and we did not come-down on the ground except together; and she undid her drawers, and they came-down into the anklets of her feet.
sentences.i: Then I reached for her waist and squeezed it, and we sank to the ground together; she loosened her drawers, and they slipped down to the anklets on her feet.
sentences.n: mā nazalnā … illā sawāʾan, “we did not go down … except alike”: we went down together. sarāwīl, “drawers, trousers”, a Persian loanword, plural in form, is treated here as a feminine singular (fa-nazalat, “and they came down”).

sentences.t: وَأَخَذْنَا فِى الْهِرَاشِ وَالتَّعْنِيقِ وَالْغُنْجِ وَالْكَلَامِ الرَّقِيقِ وَالْعَضِّ وَحَمْلِ السِّيقَانِ وَالطَّوَافِ بِالْبَيْتِ وَالْأَرْكَانِ إِلَى أَنِ ارْتَخَتْ مَفَاصِلُهَا وَغُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا وَدَخَلَتْ فِى الْغَيْبُوبَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhnā fī al-hirāshi wa-al-taʿnīqi wa-al-ghunji wa-al-kalāmi al-raqīqi wa-al-ʿaḍḍi wa-ḥamli al-sīqāni wa-al-ṭawāfi bi-al-bayti wa-al-arkāni ilā an irtakhat mafāṣiluhā wa-ghushiya ʿalayhā wa-dakhalat fī al-ghaybūbati
sentences.l: And we took-to the romping and the embracing and the coquetry and the speech the tender, and the biting, and the lifting of the legs, and the circling of the House and the corners, until her joints grew-slack, and it was fainted upon her, and she entered into the swoon.
sentences.i: And we fell to romping and embracing, to coquetry and soft words, to biting and the lifting of legs and the circling of the House and its corners, until her limbs went slack and she fainted clean away.
sentences.n: A list in the manner of rhymed prose (taʿnīq, raqīq; sīqān, arkān). al-ṭawāf bi-al-bayt wa-al-arkān, “circling the House and the corners”, takes the words for the pilgrim’s rounds of the Kaʿba and its corners as a joking figure for lovemaking; ṭāfa bi-, “go round”, takes bi-. akhadha fī, “set about, fall to”. hirāsh: rough play, romping; ghunj: a woman’s coquetry and amorous sounds; ghaybūba: a swoon. فى is printed with ى.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةُ مَسَّرَةَ الْقَلْبِ وَقُرَّةَ النَّاظِرِ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat tilka al-laylatu masarrata al-qalbi wa-qurrata al-nāẓiri kamā qāla fīhā al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And that night was the joy of the heart and the coolness of the beholder, as the poet said of it:
sentences.i: That night was the heart’s joy and the delight of the eye, as the poet said of such a night:
sentences.n: The print sets the shadda on the sīn, مسّرة; the word is masarra, “joy”, and the mark is kept where the print has it. qurrat al-nāẓir, “the coolness of the beholder”: the delight of the eye, like qurrat al-ʿayn.

sentences.t:
اَهْنَى لَيَالِي الدَّهْرِ عِنْدِي لَيْلَةٌ * لَمْ اَخْلُ فِيْهَا الْكَأْسُ مِنْ اِعْمَالِ
فَرَّقْتُ فِيْهَا بَيْنَ جَفْنِي وَالْكَرَى * وَجَمَعْتُ بَيْنَ الْقُرْطِ وَالْخَلْخَالِ
sentences.tr:
ahnā layālī al-dahri ʿindī laylatun * lam akhlu fīhā al-kaʾsu min iʿmāli
farraqtu fīhā bayna jafnī wa-al-karā * wa-jamaʿtu bayna al-qurṭi wa-al-khalkhāli
sentences.l:
The most-pleasant of the nights of time with me is a night * in which I did not leave the cup void of use;
I parted in it between my eyelid and the slumber, * and joined between the earring and the anklet.
sentences.i:
Of all the nights time ever gave, the sweetest to me * is one in which I never let the wine-cup stand idle;
all through it I kept my eyelids and sleep apart, * and brought the earring and the anklet together.
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed, including two marks that do not construe: لَمْ اَخْلُ and الْكَأْسُ in the nominative. The sense wants lam ukhli … al-kaʾsa, “I did not leave the cup empty (of use)”, and is translated so. اَهْنَى is ahnaʾ, “most pleasant”, with the hamza written as a yāʾ. The last half-line is a frank image: the woman’s ankles raised to her ears, so that anklet meets earring.

sentences.t: وَاجْتَمَعْنَا وَنِمْنَا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ وَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَرِفَ وَإِذَا بِهَا أَمْسَكَتْنِي وَقَالَتْ لِي قِفْ حَتَّى أَقُولَ لَكَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ijtamaʿnā wa-nimnā ilā al-ṣabāḥi wa-aradtu an anṣarifa wa-idhā bihā amsakatnī wa-qālat lī qif ḥattā aqūla laka ʿalā shayʾin
sentences.l: And we came-together, and slept until the morning; and I wanted to depart, and behold her — she held me fast and said to me: Stay, until I tell you about a thing.
sentences.i: We lay together and slept till morning. I wanted to leave, but she caught hold of me and said, “Wait, so that I can tell you something.”
sentences.n: qāla ʿalā, “tell about”: a spoken use of ʿalā for “concerning”. wa-idhā bihā: the bi- of surprise.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
